verdict: OK to lend in Morbi corrugated boxes and paper packaging, but only to converters with clean payment records and diversified end-customers; avoid units named in the association's non-payment list.
title: Morbi corrugated boxes & paper packaging: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A Morbi box unit buys kraft paper and liner board, runs it through a corrugator to make board, then prints, cuts and glues it into cartons for ceramic tile packers, FMCG, food and apparel. **Cash is made on conversion margin per tonne, not on paper price** — paper is a pass-through and the converter earns on yield, waste control and machine hours. Capex is modest and modular (corrugator, printer-slotter, die-cutter), so a unit can add a line in months; that also means capacity arrives fast when margins look good. Working capital is the real business: paper suppliers want short credit while tile and FMCG buyers stretch payment, so **the receivable book, not the machine, is where your money sits**.

## What has changed now
Gujarat is running ahead of the country — GST collections up 11.9% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D] — so local demand for boxes is real. But India-wide, bank credit is growing 15.5% YoY against output of 8.6% [D], and IIP for NIC 17 (paper and paper products) is at -0.1% YoY [D]: **paper-sector output is flat while credit into the chain is expanding**, which is exactly how stretched receivables build up. Locally, the Morbi Packaging Association has given units a deadline to clear dues and will blacklist non-payers, with no company supplying goods to them [3]. That is the single most useful fact in this file.

## Where the growth is
Peer results confirm demand, not distress: TCPL's Q1 FY27 consolidated total income rose 16% YoY to INR 495 crore with EBITDA up 17% to INR 88 crore [7], and its FY26 revenue was INR 1,835.56 crore with PAT of INR 97.80 crore [4][5]. UFlex reported EBITDA margin of 15.3%, the highest in 14 quarters [6]. **Pursue Morbi converters who supply tile exporters and FMCG with 3+ end-customers, hold a GST-clean record, and buy paper from mills outside the blacklist.** Avoid single-customer units tied to one tile packer, and avoid any unit appearing on the association's default list [3].

**Take stock and book-debt statements every month, plus GST returns and the paper purchase ledger** — the purchase ledger tells you real capacity use. Covenant a minimum current ratio and a cap on top-one-buyer concentration; if the top buyer crosses half of sales, ask for a diversification plan before enhancing limits. Where the unit's paper supplier credit terms are unknown, collect from customer.
